scope: shift the outbound starting sequence to 2 to match the client's incomingSequence

observed_result.why_it_did_not_take: the default argument only applies when the attribute is absent; on this connection the counter already existed (the server emits an in-band reply right after connect and again after stats), so by gamestate time it had already advanced past 2

conclusion: the sequence-offset experiment was not actually performed; the outbound start is still the natural 3 from earlier traffic
correct_approach_next: force the gamestate sequence explicitly instead of relying on the running counter (for example set a dedicated gamestate_seq attribute and use it for all fragments)
or patch conn+0x34 (incomingSequence) to 2 so the client expects 3, then resend with seq 3 - this avoids touching the server at all
note: conn+0x34 read 1 in the populated-object run, which is the basis for believing the client expects 2
